summary: In this episode, Fr. Andrew Stephen Damick reads the full text of the Harrowing of Hell from the Gospel of Nicodemus (also known as the Acts of Pilate), an apocryphal New Testament text from the 4th or 5th century. He explains that this text is not Scripture but is considered a book to be read at home, and it has influenced Orthodox liturgical texts. The narrative describes the descent of Christ into Hades after His crucifixion, where He breaks the gates of brass, defeats Satan and Death, and leads the righteous souls of the Old Testament (Adam, the patriarchs, prophets, and the penitent thief) into Paradise. The story is framed as a testimony from two sons of Simeon, Karinus and Leucius, who were raised from the dead and recount their experiences. The episode emphasizes Christ's victory over death and the liberation of the captives, a central theme in Orthodox theology.

entities.title: Jesus Christ
entities.summary: The Son of God who descends into Hades after His crucifixion to liberate the righteous dead.

entities.title: Adam
entities.summary: The first man, who is liberated from Hades by Christ and led into Paradise.

entities.title: Satan
entities.summary: The prince of death who opposes Christ but is ultimately bound and delivered to hell.

entities.title: Hell (personified)
entities.summary: A personified entity that rules over the underworld and is defeated by Christ.

entities.title: David
entities.summary: The prophet-king who prophesies Christ's victory and leads the saints in praise.

entities.title: Isaiah
entities.summary: The prophet who foretold the light shining on those in darkness.

entities.title: John the Baptist
entities.summary: The forerunner who announces Christ's arrival in Hades.

entities.title: Seth
entities.summary: Son of Adam who recounts the prophecy of Michael the Archangel about the coming of Christ.

entities.title: Michael the Archangel
entities.summary: The angel who gives prophecies to Seth and later leads the saints into Paradise.

entities.title: Penitent Thief
entities.summary: The robber crucified with Christ who is promised Paradise and enters first.

entities.title: Enoch
entities.summary: A righteous man who was translated to Paradise without dying, and will return to fight Antichrist.

entities.title: Elijah
entities.summary: A prophet taken up in a chariot of fire, who will return to fight Antichrist.

entities.title: Joseph of Arimathea
entities.summary: The man who buried Jesus and testifies to the resurrection.

entities.title: Annas and Caiaphas
entities.summary: High priests who question Joseph and later receive the testimony of Karinus and Leucius.

entities.title: Karinus and Leucius
entities.summary: Sons of Simeon who were raised from the dead and wrote the account of the Harrowing of Hell.

concepts.title: Harrowing of Hell
concepts.summary: The descent of Christ into Hades after His crucifixion to liberate the righteous souls of the Old Testament, defeating Satan and Death.

concepts.title: Gospel of Nicodemus
concepts.summary: An apocryphal New Testament text from the 4th-5th century, also known as the Acts of Pilate, which recounts the Harrowing of Hell and is used in Orthodox liturgical traditions.

concepts.title: Books Read at Home
concepts.summary: A category of Christian literature that is not Scripture but is edifying for personal reading, distinct from heretical texts.

claims.text: Christ descended into Hades after His crucifixion, broke the gates of brass, and liberated the righteous souls of the Old Testament.
The Gospel of Nicodemus is not Scripture but a book to be read at home, reflecting traditions not in the Bible.
Satan was deceived by the cross, thinking he could defeat Christ, but instead lost his power over death.
The penitent thief was the first to enter Paradise after Christ's descent, bearing the sign of the cross.

scriptural_links.summary: Quoted as 'Lift up your heads, O gates' when Christ enters Hades.
Quoted by Isaiah: 'The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.'
Quoted by Isaiah: 'O death, where is thy sting? O hell, where is thy victory?'
Quoted by Adam: 'Thou hast brought my soul out of hell.'
Quoted by David: 'Sing unto the Lord a new song...'
Quoted by Micah: 'What God is like unto thee...'
Quoted by the thief: 'Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.'

glossary.definition: The descent of Christ into Hades after His death to free the righteous souls of the Old Testament.
An apocryphal text from the 4th-5th century recounting the trial, crucifixion, and descent into Hades of Jesus.
Texts not included in the biblical canon but considered edifying for private reading.
Scripture, the first category of books used in liturgical worship.
Edifying texts not read in church but suitable for personal devotion.
